paths.title: Start Here
paths.subtitle: The essential Paul Graham essays, in order
paths.description: This path begins with choosing work, protecting focus, and thinking clearly. It then builds founder resourcefulness, startup wealth, idea discovery, unscalable beginnings, growth, and ends with a capstone on great work.

steps.note: Start here: choose making good new things over prestige, imitation, or default career paths.
Use the play-work test to find work you can sustain and eventually turn into a startup.
Protect long uninterrupted maker blocks; fragmented schedules destroy the focus great work requires.
Keep beliefs from becoming identity so you can reason clearly about contested, important questions.
Write to pressure-test vague ideas; gaps appear before you commit time or money.
Build independent-mindedness to resist conventional thinking and generate novel ideas worth pursuing.
The core founder trait: adapt relentlessly around obstacles rather than making excuses or quitting.
Understand why startups create wealth: small teams, hard problems, and measurable performance earn leverage.
Notice problems you urgently need; build rough versions and follow narrow users before broad markets.
Recruit first users manually, delight them intensely, and use unscalable tactics to spark growth.
Use weekly growth as the compass; without it, startup decisions lose their clearest test.
Capstone: choose important problems, cultivate curiosity, and sustain effort across a career of great work.

paths.title: For Founders
paths.subtitle: Idea to first customers, in order
paths.description: A first-time founder's arc from choosing to start through finding an idea, building a first version, launching, and landing early users. Each essay is practical and still true today, ordered so each builds on the last.

steps.note: Start here: why ambitious builders should own their work rather than take a safe big-company job.
Dismantles the common excuses that keep you from starting, so you commit instead of deliberating.
Once committed: learn domain expertise, pick cofounders by trust, and let ideas emerge from curiosity.
Now find an idea by noticing problems you urgently need, not inventing plausible-sounding ones.
Deepens idea-finding by surfacing the unpleasant schleps your unconscious avoids.
Refines the search: build from what's broken in your own life, especially early on.
Before building, adopt the core founder trait: relentless resourcefulness in the face of obstacles.
A compact checklist for the build phase: understand users, launch fast, stay cheap.
Launch tactic: recruit your first users manually and delight them with unscalable effort.
With users in hand, focus weekly on the one problem blocking growth and iterate on feedback.
Measure weekly growth as the compass for every decision once you have traction.
Finally, know if you're default alive or dead, and avoid overhiring before you're sure.
